text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said the country was not planning any direct devaluation of its currency, the crown.

- Jan Ducky, director of the state-owned gas distribution monopoly SPP, said new contracts between SPP and Russian Gazprom would save Slovakia "tens of millions of dollars" through lower prices and higher quality gas.
- Slovakia will on Monday officially announce to the Czech Republic the introduction of quotas on import of Czech beer.
- Local money market dealers said the central bank has succeded in its fight for a stable currency, saying the market last week registered foreign sales of crowns.

PRAVDA - Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic said his recent visit to the U.S. confirmed that Slovakia was not likely to be included in the first wave of NATO enlargement, but added that Bratislava should get a chance in future expansion rounds.
- An extraordinary session of parliament, called by the opposition to seek the dismissal of Interior Minister Gustav Krajci, should be held by next Thursday.
SME - Opposition Christian Democratic Union (KDU) leader Jan Carnogursky said Slovakia did not have a chance to be invited to the first round of integration talks with the European Union (EU).
- Carnogursky said that talks between the ruling coalition and opposition would not increase chances for early membership in the EU.

- Jozef Migas, leader of the opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said the most important issue on the agenda of a potential meeting between coalition and opposition would be a law on direct presidential elections.
PRACA - Drivers of Bratislava public transport company on Saturday interrupted their protest strike which had paralyzed the city's transport over the last few days.
